speeding among those who hasten, straight-flying as he rushes forward, scatters dust above his brows.
And indeed, at his thundering like that of heaven, those who attack him tremble in fear;
when he fights against a thousand, he becomes irresistible and terrible as he advances.
And indeed, people praise his speed—the swift overcomer of the peoples—and they say of him as he departs from the fray:
"Dadhikrā has sped away with thousands."
Dadhikrā has spread across the five peoples with his power, as the sun spreads light over the waters.
May the prize-winning steed, winner of thousands and hundreds, fill these words with honey-sweetness.
Let us now praise that swift Dadhikrā; let us celebrate him who belongs to heaven and earth.
May the dawning Dawns inspire me; may they carry me across all difficulties.
I celebrate the great deeds of the steed Dadhikrāvan, the bull of many boons, who fulfills our intentions—
him whom you two, O Mitra and Varuṇa, bestowed upon the Pūrus as a radiant and victorious one, like Agni.
May Aditi, in harmony with Mitra and Varuṇa, make him sinless who has offered praise to the horse Dadhikrāvan when the fire is kindled at the dawning of the Uṣas.
We have meditated upon the food and the great strength of Dadhikrāvan, and the auspicious name of the Maruts.
For our well-being, we invoke Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni, and Indra, whose arm wields the thunderbolt.
Like Indra, both sides invoke him as they rise up and proceed toward the sacrifice;
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you two have granted us the horse Dadhikrā, the benefactor for mortals.
I have celebrated Dadhikrāvan, the victorious, the spirited steed.
May he make our mouths fragrant; may he prolong our lives.
Now let us celebrate Dadhikrāvan; may all the dawns quicken me—the [quickening] of the waters, of Agni, of the Dawn, of Sūrya, and of Bṛhaspati, the victorious son of Aṅgiras.
May the being who nourishes, who seeks cattle, who is to be served, hasten toward glory;
may he, the winner of food at the break of dawn, the true one, the swift runner, the mover, the bird-like flyer, Dadhikrāvan, produce food, strength, and light.
And indeed, as he runs and hastens, eager for the prize, the wind blows after him like the wing of a bird;
as Dadhikrāvan speeds along, he overcomes the curves of the path with his might, like a swooping falcon.
And this vigorous steed, bound by the neck, at the flanks, and in the mouth, hastens toward the whip;
Dadhikrā, having exerted his strength, has leaped along the curves of the paths.
The swan dwelling in the pure realm, the Vasu dwelling in the mid-air, the Hotṛ-priest dwelling at the altar, the guest dwelling in the house;

dwelling among men, dwelling in the best of places, dwelling in Truth, dwelling in the firmament; born of the waters, born of the kine, born of Truth, born of the mountains—He is the Eternal Law (Ṛta).
O Indra and Varuṇa, what hymn accompanied by oblations has reached you for favor— like an immortal Hotar-priest—
that inspired prayer, uttered by us with reverence, may touch your hearts, O Indra and Varuṇa?

The mortal who, providing sacrificial food, has made Indra and Varuṇa his two divine allies for friendship—he slays the Vṛtras and his enemies in battles; through their great protections, he becomes renowned.
Indra and Varuṇa are indeed the most liberal bestowers of treasure upon men who labor for them;
when they, as friends for friendship's sake, delight themselves with pressed Soma juices and abundant nourishment.
O Indra and Varuṇa, you two fierce ones, hurl your most powerful missile, the thunderbolt, against him who is evil toward us, the wolf-like Dabhīti; measure out your overwhelming might upon him.
O Indra and Varuṇa, may you two become the lovers of this prayer, like two bulls of a cow. May she yield for us like a great cow that has gone to pasture, pouring forth a thousand streams of milk.
For our offspring, for our well-placed progeny, for fertile fields, for the sight of the sun, and for manly heroism—
may Indra and Varuṇa be our protectors here with their aids, O wonder-workers, in the decisive struggle.

For it is you two alone, the abundant ones, who are well-disposed toward us for our ancient protection in the quest for cattle; O heroes, most generous and bringing happiness like parents, we choose you for our dear friendship.

These prayers of ours, seeking strength for your protection, have gone forth like racers longing for you, O bounteous givers. Like cows approaching the soma for its glory, my hymns and thoughts have come to Indra and Varuṇa.
These inspirations of mine have gone forth to Indra and Varuṇa, desiring wealth;
they have approached them like those seeking to please for the sake of riches, like swift mares seeking a share of glory.

May we ourselves be masters of wealth consisting of horses, chariots, and prosperity—of our own enduring riches. May those [gods], performing their aid with ever-newer succors, attend us with yoked teams of wealth.
O Great Ones, come to us with your great aids, O Indra and Varuṇa, for the winning of the prize;
when the flashing arrows play in the battles, may we be the winners of that contest through you both.
Twice has the kingdom been mine, the Kṣatriya’s, as all the immortals have willed it for us.
The gods follow the will of Varuṇa; I rule over the people, the highest enclosure.
I am King Varuṇa; these first divine powers were established for me. The gods follow the will of Varuṇa; I rule over the people of the highest enclosure.
I am Indra and Varuṇa through our greatness; the two vast, deep, well-established realms are mine.
Like Tvaṣṭṛ, knowing all beings, I have brought the two worlds together and uphold them.
I caused the swelling waters to flow; I supported heaven in the seat of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*).
By means of *ṛta*, the son of Aditi, a guardian of *ṛta*, has spread out the earth in its threefold extent.
Men with fine horses, seeking booty, call upon me when they are hemmed in by the enemy in battle;
I, Indra, the bounteous one, create the fray, raising up the dust with my overwhelming might.
I have performed all these deeds; no divine power can restrain me, the irresistible one.
When the Soma juices exhilarate me and when I am praised with hymns, both the boundless realms of space tremble in fear.
All beings know you as such; you proclaim those deeds to Varuṇa, O Ordainer.
You are renowned for having slain the Vṛtras; you, Indra, have set free the obstructed rivers.
Our fathers were here, those seven seers, when Durgaha was being bound;
they sacrificed for Trasadasyu through her, like Indra the subduer of Vṛtra, the demi-god.
For Purukutsānī served you both with oblations and with homages, O Indra and Varuṇa;
therefore, you two gave her King Trasadasyu, the slayer of Vṛtra, the demi-god.
May we, having won wealth, rejoice with it, as the gods do with oblations and cattle with pasture;
O Indra and Varuṇa, grant us every day that cow who never fails us.
Who will hear us? Which one among those worthy of sacrifice? Which god will take pleasure in our praise?
To whose heart shall we offer this divine, most beloved hymn of beautiful praise, accompanied by excellent oblations, among the immortals?

Who will show mercy? Which one will come most readily? And which among the gods is the most beneficent? Whose chariot do they call swift with its racing horses—the one whom the daughter of the Sun chose?
For you two come swiftly on such days as these, like Indra exerting his power in the decisive encounter.
Born from heaven, divine birds of beautiful wings—by what power among powers do you become most mighty?
What kind of approach has been for you? By what means, O Aśvins, do you come when you are invoked?
Who among us, even in the face of great abandonment, have you protected? O Madhvīs, O Dasras, grant us your aid!

Wide through the sky your chariot reaches, as it turns back from the ocean toward you. O lovers of sweetness, they sprinkle honey for you; when they have prepared for you the cooked sacrificial foods.
The Sindhu indeed sprinkled your horses with the Rasa; the ruddy birds flew around in the heat.
That swift vehicle of yours was well-known, by which you became the two husbands of Sūryā.
Whatever I have here and there offered to you both together, may this be for us a benevolent favor, O you whose treasure is booty. Protect the singer; for our desire, O Nāsatyas, is fixed upon you.
O Aśvins, we invoke today that chariot of yours which has wide-reaching power, the gathering-place of the kine;
it which bears Sūryā, whose seat is full of life, which carries the singer, and which is most frequently sought after for wealth.
O Aśvins, sons of Heaven, you win that glory through your divine powers and your deeds; nourishments attend your wondrous form when your lofty steeds draw your chariot.
Who today, having offered oblations with hymns, will bring you both for aid or for the drinking of the pressed juice?
Or who, offering homage, will turn you, O Aśvins, toward the ancient lover of the *ṛta*?
O Nāsatyas, you who exist in many places, come to this sacrifice with your golden chariot;
drink of the honeyed Soma and bestow treasure upon the person who honors you.
Come to us from heaven and from earth upon your golden, well-rolling chariot!
Let not other seekers of the gods detain you, for our ancient kinship with you has been established.
Now, O Wonder-Workers, measure out for us great wealth consisting of many heroes among both our groups;
since the men who belong to the line of Ajamīḷha have brought hymns of praise to you, O Aśvins, they have come to this joint song of praise.

Whatever I have here and there offered to you both together, may this be a source of favor for us, O you whose treasure is booty! Protect the singer; for our desire, O Nāsatyas, is directed toward you.
This very light rises up; the chariot is harnessed, the traveler upon the ridge of this heaven.
Within it are three nourishing pairs; the fourth, the leather bag, overflows with honey.
Your food-offerings, rich in sweetness, rise up; your chariots and horses [speed] at the dawning of the Uṣas.
Uncovering the darkness that enveloped it, they spread the bright light through the mid-air like the sun.
Drink of the honey with your honey-drinking mouths; moreover, harness your dear chariot for the sake of the honey.
You quicken the tracks and the paths with honey; O Aśvins, you carry a honey-filled skin.

The swans that carry you—sweet, unfailing, golden-winged, swift, and awakening at dawn; plunging into the waters, exhilarating, and touching the exhilarating draught—you come to the libations like flies to honey.
The fires, with well-performed sacrifices and rich in sweetness, awaken at dawn for the Aśvins;
when the skillful and far-sighted one, with cleansed hands, has pressed the honeyed Soma with the stones.
The seekers of the light, shaking off [darkness] through the days, extend the bright sky across the mid-air like the sun;
even as the sun yokes his horses, he moves along, while you two, by your own power, perceive all paths.

O Aśvins, I have proclaimed for you this prayer-inspiring hymn: that chariot of yours which has good horses and is ageless, by which you traverse the regions in an instant toward the one who brings the oblation, the swift and generous patron.
Drink first of the pressed sweet juices, O Vāyu, at the sacrifices;
for you are the one who drinks first.
O Vāyu, with your hundred aids, accompanied by your teams and with Indra as your charioteer, sate yourselves with the pressed soma.
O Indra and Vāyu, may a thousand bay horses bring you both toward the offerings to drink the Soma.
O Indra and Vāyu, come to the chariot with its golden seat, which is well-worshipped and touches the heavens. For you both shall mount it.
Come to the donor with your chariot of broad splendor;
O Indra and Vāyu, come here!
O Indra and Vāyu, this [soma] has been pressed; being in harmony with the gods, drink it in the house of the donor.
O Indra and Vāyu, let your journey be here, your unyoking here;
may you come here for the drinking of the Soma.
O Vāyu, the bright first portion of the honeyed mead is offered to you at the sacrifices;
come, O desirable god, with your team of horses, for the drinking of the Soma.
O Indra and Vāyu, you two deserve the drinking of these Soma juices;
for toward you the drops flow together, like waters descending to the lowlands.
O Vāyu and Indra, you two impetuous lords of power, come on the same chariot with your teams of horses for our protection, to drink the Soma.
O Heroes, Indra and Vāyu, those many-desired teams of yours which belong to the donor— bestow them upon us, you who bring the sacrifice.
Accept the invocations; let them reach the wealth of the noble one like inspired songs.
O Vāyu, come on your shining chariot to drink of the pressed soma.
Driving away those who revile us, O Vāyu, accompanied by your team and with Indra as your charioteer, come on your shining chariot to drink of the pressed soma.
The two dark treasuries of wealth, adorned with every ornament, have followed along;
O Vāyu, come on your shining chariot to drink of the pressed soma.
May ninety-nine horses, yoked by thought, carry you;
O Vāyu, come on your shining chariot to drink of the pressed soma.
O Vāyu, harness a hundred bay steeds, well-fed and vigorous; or let your chariot come hither with its thousandfold power.
O Indra and Bṛhaspati, this dear oblation is placed in your mouth;
the hymn of praise and the exhilarating draught are recited.
O Indra and Bṛhaspati, this Soma is poured out for you both—
delightful for exhilaration and for drinking.
O Indra and Bṛhaspati, come to our house; O Soma-drinkers, come for the drinking of the Soma.
O Indra and Bṛhaspati, bestow upon us wealth consisting of hundreds,
consisting of thousands, and abounding in horses.
O Indra and Bṛhaspati, we invoke you with songs when the Soma is pressed,
for the drinking of this Soma.
O Indra and Bṛhaspati, drink the Soma in the house of the donor; rejoice there, you who dwell in that same abode.
Bṛhaspati, who with his might suddenly propped apart the ends of the earth, he who dwells in the three stations by his roar—
him, the sweet-tongued one, the ancient seers, the inspired sages, gazing upon him, have established in front.
O Bṛhaspati, may those who, rushing forward with a great banner and rejoicing, have assailed us— protect the spotted,
flowing, inviolable, wide space, and the womb of this [sacrifice].
O Bṛhaspati, from that which is the furthest distance, those who touch the cosmic order have descended hither.
For you, the wells dug out and milked by the stones drip honey on every side in abundance.
Bṛhaspati, being first born from the great light in the highest heaven,
seven-mouthed and many-born, blew away the darkness with his roar and his seven rays.
With his well-praising, hymn-chanting host, Bṛhaspati shattered Vala and the Phaliga with a roar; bellowing aloud, he drove out the lowing, milk-yielding cows.

Thus let us serve the Father, the bull who belongs to all the gods, with sacrifices, with homage, and with oblations. O Bṛhaspati, may we, possessing good offspring and heroic sons, become masters of riches.
He indeed, as king, stands over all hostile armies by his might and his heroic power— he who maintains Bṛhaspati well-nourished, praises him, and honors him as the one who receives the first share.
He indeed dwells well-established in his own home; for him *Iḷā* swells at all times.
To that king in whose presence the Brahman goes before him, the subjects bow down of their own accord.
Unopposed, he conquers the wealth of his enemies as well as that of his own people—the king who creates wide space for the priest seeking his aid; him the gods protect.

O Indra and Bṛhaspati, drink the Soma, rejoicing at this sacrifice, O you who possess bull-like wealth! May the self-sustaining drops enter you both; bestow upon us wealth consisting of all heroic sons.
O Bṛhaspati and Indra, prosper us together; let that benevolence of yours be with us.
Favor our prayers, awaken the abundant thoughts, and exhaust the hostilities of the enemy and of those who would attack us.
This very light, most abundant, has risen in the east from out of the darkness, making the way clear.
Now may the daughters of heaven, the dawns, shining brightly, create a path for the people.
The brilliant Dawns have stood in the east like sacrificial posts set up for the rites;
shining forth, they have opened wide the two doors of the enclosure of darkness—pure and purifying.
Shining forth today, may the wealthy Dawns awaken the liberal patrons for the sake of bestowing gifts;
let the stingy misers sleep on within the darkness, unawakened in the midst of gloom.

O Goddesses, will that ancient or new journey of yours, O Dawns, be with us today? With that [journey] by which you, the wealthy ones, shone forth richly for Navagva, Aṅgira, and Daśagva at the seven-mouthed [fire], so shine now.

For you, O goddesses, with your horses yoked by the Eternal Law (*ṛta*), traverse all worlds in an instant; O Dawns, awakening the sleeping, you rouse every living being, both biped and quadruped, to movement.
Where indeed is that one, which among them is the ancient, by whose ordinance they fashioned the forms of the Ṛbhus?
As the radiant Dawns move toward beauty, they are not distinguished, being alike and ageless.
Truly, those auspicious Dawns were indeed present in the past—those whose splendor was manifest, who are born of Truth and are true;
at whose arrival the sacrificer, striving with hymns, praising and reciting, immediately obtained wealth.
They move together from the east, spreading out from the same place;
awakening from the seat of Order (*ṛta*), the goddesses Dawn break forth like herds of cows.
These very Dawns, alike and uniform, move on with their unimpaired colors;
hiding the black monster with their radiant bodies, they are bright, pure, and shining.
O divine daughters of heaven, shining forth, bestow upon us wealth accompanied by progeny. Awakening from your pleasant presence, may we be masters of heroic vigor.
O Dawns, daughters of heaven, shining forth, I address you, whose banner is the sacrifice:
may we be glorious among the people; may Heaven and the goddess Earth grant us this.
This noble lady, shining forth, has appeared from her sister;
the daughter of heaven has been seen.
Like a dappled mare, ruddy and true to the cosmic order, Dawn, the mother of cattle, has become the friend of the Aśvins.
Moreover, you are the friend of the Aśvins, and you are the mother of the cows;
and, O Uṣas, you rule over wealth.
O you who ward off hatred, O possessor of true abundance, we have awakened you with our hymns of praise through our conscious awareness.
The auspicious rays have appeared like herds of cattle;
Dawn has filled the wide expanse.
O radiant one, having filled [the world], you have dispelled the darkness with your light;
O Uṣas, favor us according to your own nature.
O Uṣas, with your bright radiance, you extend across the sky, the wide and beloved intermediate space, and the atmosphere with your beams.
We choose that great and desirable gift of the divine Savitṛ, the wise Asura;
by which he himself bestows protection upon the donor—may the Great God grant that to us through his nights.
The upholder of heaven, Prajāpati, the lord of creatures, the seer, puts on his tawny mantle. Far-seeing, spreading out and filling the wide space, Savitṛ has generated praiseworthy bliss.

He has filled the celestial and terrestrial realms; the God makes his fame known for his own law. Savitar has stretched out his arms to impel the world, laying it to rest and setting it in motion by means of the nights.

Unassailable, surveying all beings, the god Savitṛ protects the sacred laws. He has stretched out his arms for the creatures of the world; upholding the vows, he rules over the great course of the universe.
Savitar thrice through his greatness pervades the mid-air; he encompasses the three regions and the three luminous spheres.
He impels the three heavens and the three earths; by means of his three laws, he protects us with his own self.

Possessing great bounty, the impeller, the one who brings rest to both the moving and the stationary, he who is the lord of both— may that god Savitar grant us protection, a triple-layered refuge from distress for our dwelling.

The God has come with the seasons; may he increase our dwelling. May Savitṛ grant us food and good offspring. May he quicken us through nights and days, and may he bestow upon us wealth accompanied by progeny.

The god Savitṛ has now become worthy of our praise; he is to be invoked by men at this time of day—he who distributes treasures to human beings, so that he may grant us the most excellent wealth here.
For you first bestow upon the worshipful gods immortality as their supreme portion;
then, O Savitṛ, you unfold the gift for humanity, providing successive spans of life.
Whatever we have done without intent against the divine folk, through feeble skill, through lack of power, or through human frailty—
O Savitṛ, among both gods and men, do you here impel us to be sinless.
That power of the divine Savitṛ cannot be measured, by which he shall sustain the entire world—
that which the skillful-fingered one brings forth truly upon the breadth of the earth and the height of heaven, that is his truth.
To the great mountains, you bring as dwellings those who have Indra as their chief and who possess household abodes;
however they may fly apart, O Savitṛ, they stand still at your impulsion.
O Savitṛ, those impulses of yours which three times a day, day after day, bring us prosperity—
may Indra, Heaven and Earth, Sindhu with her waters, and Aditi with the Ādityas, grant us protection.

Who is your protector, O Vasus? Who is your defender? O Heaven and Earth, O Aditi, protect us from the more powerful mortal, O Varuṇa and Mitra! O Gods, who among you will grant wide space at our sacrifice?
They who shall sing forth the ancient ordinances when they shine out as their illuminators, unerring;
those ordainers have distributed them, the tireless ones whose thoughts are fixed on *Ṛta*, the wonder-workers who have shone forth.
With hymns, I invoke for friendship the goddess Aditi, the dwelling, and the Sindhu river—Svastī—for protection.
May both Uṣas and Night, the undeceivable ones, cause day and night to fall upon us so that we may be safe.
Aryaman and Varuṇa have made the path clear; Agni, the lord of nourishment, has made a way for prosperity.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, being well-praised, grant us manly protection and mighty shelter.
I have invoked the protections of Parvata, of the Maruts, and of the divine savior Bhaga.
May the Lord protect us from the distress caused by strangers, and may Mitra deliver us from the harm of those who act as friends.
Now let the two goddesses, Rodasī, be praised by the Dragon of the Deep with these desired libations;
like those seeking gain on a journey to the ocean, the rivers, flowing with the heat of the sun, have uncovered their waters.
May the goddess Aditi protect us with the gods; may the god Trātṛ save us, never failing. For we ought not to violate the ordinance of Mitra and Varuṇa, nor the ridge of Agni.
Agni is the lord of wealth; Agni is the lord of great fortune. May he bestow those things upon us.
O bountiful Dawn, O giver of joy, bring hither many desirable things for us, O lady rich in prizes.
May Savitar, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, and Indra come to us with that gift of ours.
O mighty Heaven and Earth, you two most excellent ones, be present here with your splendor through your radiant hymns;
when the bull, building up the two vast and wide expanses, bellows with his far-reaching movements.
The two goddesses, honored by the gods who are worthy of sacrifice, stand unaging and swelling;
they are observers of cosmic order, free from guile, mothers of the gods, leaders of the sacrifice with their radiant hymns.

He indeed was the skillful craftsman among the worlds, he who brought forth these two, heaven and earth; the wise one, by his power, established the two wide and deep realms, well-fashioned and without support.
Now may Rodasī, together with her husband, rejoicing and bestowing nourishment, protect us with her vast and great defenses;
O all-pervading and holy ones, guard us through our prayer, and may we ever be chariot-riders who win the prize.
We bring forth our great hymn of praise to you two, O Heaven and Earth, the pure ones, for your glorification.
Purifying each other’s bodies, you rule by your own inherent power;
from of old, you have been carried forth according to the Eternal Law.
O great ones, you accomplish the *ṛta* of Mitra, crossing over and fulfilling it;
you have both taken your seats around the sacrifice.
Through the Lord of the Field, as if with a friend, may we conquer;
may he, who nourishes cattle and horses, be gracious to us for such a purpose.
O Lord of the Field, pour out for us a wave rich in sweetness, as a cow yields her milk—sweet-dropping, well-purified like clarified butter. May the Lords of Eternal Order be gracious unto us.
May the plants be honey-sweet, may the heavens and the waters be so; may the mid-region be honey-sweet for us.
May the Lord of the Field be honey-sweet for us; may we follow him unharmed.
May the draft-animals be auspicious, may the men be auspicious; may the plough furrow auspiciously.
May the leather thongs be bound auspiciously; may you raise the goad auspiciously.
O Śuna and Sīra, may you both take pleasure in this speech; with that milk which you created in heaven, sprinkle upon this earth.
Turn toward us, O auspicious Sītā; we revere you, so that you may be fortunate for us, so that you may bear us good fruit.
May Indra take hold of the furrow; may Pūṣan guide it.
May she, rich in milk, yield for us through each succeeding year.
May our ploughshares furrow the earth for our welfare; may the plowmen go forth happily with their draft-animals.
May Parjanya bless us with honeyed waters; O Śuna and Sīra, bestow prosperity upon us!
From the ocean a wave rich in sweetness has arisen; through the *upāṃśu* cup it has attained immortality.
That which is the secret name of clarified butter is the tongue of the gods, the navel of immortality.
Let us proclaim our names; let us offer this oblation of clarified butter at this sacrifice with our homages.
May the Brahman priest hear the hymn being recited; the four-horned bull has bellowed this.
Four are his horns, three are his feet, two are his heads, and seven are his hands.
Bound in three ways, the bull bellows; the great god has entered into mortals.
The gods discovered the clarified butter (ghṛta) hidden in three places within the cow, concealed by the Paṇis.
Indra produced one part, Sūrya produced one, and they fashioned one from Vena by their own inherent power.
These [streams] flow from the heart-ocean, moving in a hundred channels, unobserved by the enemy.
I behold the streams of clarified butter; in their midst stands the golden reed.
The streams flow perfectly like rivers, being purified within by the heart and the mind;
these waves of clarified butter surge forth like wild beasts fleeing from a swift bowman.
Like the swift currents of a river on its course, the mighty streams fly forth, overtaking the wind;
the streams of clarified butter flow like a ruddy steed, bursting through the barriers and swelling with waves.
Like beautiful women smiling as they go to a gathering, the streams of clarified butter have approached Agni as kindling-wood; finding pleasure in them, Jātavedas eagerly accepts them.
Like maidens adorning themselves for the bridal procession, I gaze upon the ointments being applied;
where the Soma is pressed and where the sacrifice is performed, there the streams of clarified butter flow down in purification.
Flow toward our excellent praise in the contest for cattle; bestow auspicious riches upon us.
Lead this sacrifice of ours to the gods; the streams of clarified butter flow sweetly as they purify themselves.
Upon your abode the entire world is supported: within the ocean, within the heart, and within life.
May we attain that honeyed wave of yours, which is brought forth at the meeting-point on the surface of the waters.
